doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Rejoining Benny Goodman after discharge
summary: Leaving the Navy, discharge points, joining Goodman, and the Navy bassist.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Okay, so after World War II, did you stay on the east coast or did you eventually move out.
I joined Benny Goodman immediately. I got out the 9th of October in 19 — what year was this?

‘45. And I went back to North Carolina to see my mother for a couple of days or something. But I had the job with Benny, I think the 15th or something like that. And I was with Benny until he broke up the band in fourteen months. And I was very happy to © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

join that band after three years in the Navy. Because four of us went out of that band. The band, we were not all, they discharged — the married guys got out first, they had more points. So they didn’t know it but I was divorced at about that same time. If they’d have found out I’d probably still be in the Navy.
You said something about points? You had to have a certain number of points?
Okay. And if you were married—
Overseas counted more than home. So we were overseas two out of the three years we were out of the country. You got a little more money, sixteen dollars a month or something, for travel time.
Well when you joined Goodman, Gene Krupa was probably gone by then.
Maurice, oh no, I can’t — he died. Morey Feld.

Well four of us joined, there was the bass player, Barney Kessel — not Barney Kessel — Barney Spieler, was our bass player. Later on he got killed in an auto accident in Holland, he had moved to Holland and was playing in a symphony there and he was killed. That was the bass player in the Navy band.
